observed: One shared horizontal water-air interface; irregular horizontal water hatching fills the lower region. It is not a lattice or a measured curve.
One point light source S beneath the surface, near the center.
Thirteen upward incident directions are visible: a vertical direction and six oblique directions to either side.
Nine upward transmitted directions are visible: the vertical direction and four to either side, with the outer transmitted pair almost grazing.

Reflected directions point downward in the water, including the downward central arrow sharing the normal line; the two outer oblique directions on each side do not have upward transmitted continuations.
The near-grazing transmitted rays are thinner than the nearer-normal transmitted rays; the outer reflected directions are stronger/thicker.
Only the source label S is printed. No angles, distances, index labels, percentages, axes or ticks are given.
limits: Individual printed slopes and stroke widths are qualitative. Neither Fresnel coefficients nor precise energy values are observed.
Some reflected traces terminate close to the interface; these are direction indicators, not observed endpoints of propagation.
textBoundRequirements: A source lies a short distance below water. Higher-index water is first medium; air is second.
Stronger light is shown by thicker rays, with no claim that visual brightness is an energy measurement.
Preserve the normal, subcritical, nearly grazing and supercritical families in the same frame.
modernAdditions: Symmetric straight-ray layout is regularized and obeys the prose's refraction law using the already-stated approximate water index internally.
Representative ray positions and line weights are deliberately illustrative, not measured source coordinates or energy fractions.
A pale water region replaces engraving; all source families remain, including the weak central downward reflection.
English Air, Water, Thicker rays: stronger light and Modern schematic labels and explicit arrowheads are modern additions.
